newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: Kazakh blue chips to meet major investors in June.
newsitem.headline: Kazakh blue chips to meet major investors in June.

text.p: Kazakhstan holds an investment conference in June where the oil-rich republic's blue chip companies will have a chance to meet major foreign investors.

"On June 18-20...Kazakhstan will hold a conference for investors. We expect active participation of foreigners wishing to invest in our market," Securities Commission Chairman Grigory Marchenko told a news conference on Wednesday.
He said the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development and the International Finance Corporation -- a commercial unit of the World Bank -- had helped organise the conference.
"This is the first serious event for foreign investors on Kazakhstan's stock market," he said.

Marchenko said the Kazakh government expected 25 investment banks from the West and the Far East, as well as at least 50 foreign institutional investors, such as investment and pension funds, to take part.
Officials in Kazakhstan expect a viable stock market to be operating by the year-end.
The government has designated over 50 blue chip companies in the energy and processing sectors and says state-owned stakes of up to 39 percent will be offered.

Marchenko said the government was negotiating with leading accounting companies, including Arthur Andersen, KPMG, Ernst & Young, Deloitte Touche, Price Waterhouse and Coopers & Lybrand, on terms for auditing the blue chips.
